Critically, If this withdrawal is later cancelled BEFORE calling processL1Withdrawals, the withdrawal request is deleted on L2(StakingManager), but the corresponding L1 operation to undelegate to staker remains in the queue. safety.text: Cancelling a pending withdrawal should prevent the corresponding L1 undelegate operation from later being executed, so each stake yields at most one withdrawal.
safety.derivation: Program synthesis from the selected intent and logical pattern.
evidence: When a user queues a withdrawal, the StakingManager queues an L1 operation to withdraw HYPE from validators. Critically, If this withdrawal is later cancelled BEFORE calling processL1Withdrawals, the withdrawal request is deleted on L2(StakingManager), but the corresponding L1 operation to undelegate to staker remains in the queue. This can lead to a desynchronization between L2 state and L1 states.

Notice that this function only updates L2 state by removing the withdrawal request and returning kHYPE tokens to the user. However, it does not have a mechanism to know whether the undelegate request is still queued.
Hence, When the operator later processes the L1 operations queue with processL1Operations, all operations including those from cancelled withdrawals will be executed.

limitations: Conservation is stated at the ETH amount level: withdrawn ETH must not exceed staked ETH (1 ETH).
The report's desynchronization and HYPE-over-withdrawal impacts are not formalized in this plan.
The impact is stated as potential ('can potentially withdraw more HYPE'), so the conservation violation is formalized as withdrawn_hype > deposited_hype rather than a concrete numeric excess.
Caller authorization for cancelWithdrawal and processL1Operations is not established by the report and is not part of this claim.
The desynchronization impact is encoded as a report-grounded Boolean because no numeric L1/L2 state quantities are supplied.
The plan formalizes only the l1_l2_desync impact; the double-withdrawal and excess-HYPE impacts are not covered here.
